newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-ANI sees improved operating result.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-ANI sees improved operating result.

text.p: Australian National Industries Ltd (ANI) managing director Peter Stancliffe said on Tuesday he expected the company to report an improved operating result in the 1996/97 year.
ANI said also that it did not see any further writedown of its environmental engineering unit, the Holter group.

"Economic activity in Australia as far as we can tell looks pretty flat. However, we expect that we will improve our results, but they won't be on the back of improved activity rather they'll be the result of our own improvement programme," Stancliffe told Reuters in a telephone interview. "I'm talking about operating results."
Earlier, ANI reported an operating profit of A$22.99 million for the year to June 30, 1996, down from A$105.62 million previously.
It booked a net loss of A$213.19 million compared to a profit of A$80.38 million in 1994/95.
The result included an abnormal A$198.55 million loss, largely stemming from its A$233.55 million writedown of Holter's assets.

Asked if there were any further writedowns to come, Stancliffe said: "Not that we're aware of at this stage, although in the final wash-up there may be some slight profits and losses depending on which businesses attract how much an offer or whatever.
"We think that at the end of the day, the wash up of all of that might be a zero-sum game."
The company hoped to make an announcement regarding the future of Holter by September 30, he said.

Asked if ANI planned to offload any businesses other than Holter, Stancliffe said: "We will dispose of Container Care ... and there's a few smaller businesses that, whilst they may be performing reasonably well, they may lack critical mass. I'm thinking of some geographies in particular which may not fit into the portfolio going forward, but they're relatively small."
ANI shares closed one cent down at A$1.01.
